sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Bidens cernua is an annual of wetlands across much of the Northern Hemisphere, growing along ponds, marshes and muddy shores. Plants range roughly 10–100 cm tall, with opposite simple leaves and yellow daisy-like heads. Mature flower heads often nod, especially as the hooked achenes develop.

sections.title: Image and uses
sections.text: The plate's simple leaves and yellow radiate heads fit the species, but all heads appear upright; that can reflect the flowering stage, since ripe heads commonly droop. No food use or toxicity finding was sufficiently verified for this profile.
